Procrastination isn't a time problem. It's a feeling problem.
Up to one in five adults procrastinates chronically.
The task makes you feel bored, anxious, or not good enough.
So your brain grabs the fastest relief it can find.
One more video. One more scroll. I'll do it later.
Later turns into guilt. Guilt turns into more avoiding.
But here's the part nobody tells you.
Students who forgave themselves for procrastinating did it less on the next exam.
Shame doesn't fix it. Starting does.
Open the file. Write one line. Set a two-minute timer.
Then decide exactly when: after coffee, at my desk, I begin.
You don't need to feel ready. You just need to begin.
Every time you start, you prove that feeling wrong.
Pause this video. Do two minutes. Right now.
